<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via zodIssuesToFields (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldErrorSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `zodIssuesToFields (6 routes)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4caa238b3c55e39697dac6aef5b0eb504f08389c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f1a6b6da958e8dec63e1168c1c475127ee7f81f7` — the merge of head `1d4cdc52fe5dcbcdca4fa3196a474e8d4c20838f` into base `4caa238b3c55e39697dac6aef5b0eb504f08389c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f1a6b6da958e8dec63e1168c1c475127ee7f81f7 && git checkout f1a6b6da958e8dec63e1168c1c475127ee7f81f7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4caa238b3c55e39697dac6aef5b0eb504f08389c 1d4cdc52fe5dcbcdca4fa3196a474e8d4c20838f && git checkout -B drift-repro 4caa238b3c55e39697dac6aef5b0eb504f08389c && git merge --no-ff 1d4cdc52fe5dcbcdca4fa3196a474e8d4c20838f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4caa238b3c55e39697dac6aef5b0eb504f08389c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4caa238b3c55e39697dac6aef5b0eb504f08389c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `508fb649911cb381a50f4c2fde0988592667384c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/index.ts, packages/spec/src/api/zod-issues-to-fields.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-shape.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-save-door-refusals.ts, packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/refusal-head.ts + packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts, packages/types/src/validation-failure.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/api.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, packages/spec/export-origins/api.json

Reviewed first at `bd2bd3a6`, then re-pointed: `bd2bd3a6..508fb649` is one commit touching only `.changeset/32279-data-door-refusal-heads.md` (spec `patch` to `minor`, `Metadata-protocol: none` to `added`), verified with `git diff --stat`. The code judged below is byte-identical on both heads. Inputs: card #32279 and its five comments (triage 6773702059, claim 6775517584, os-dev-report 6777368093, claim correction 6777418296), the PR body as it stands now, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on `508fb649`.

Gates on `508fb649` at the time of writing:
- Green: Check Changeset (the re-run 130081113030; the earlier run 130080523581 on this head failed because it read the PR body while it still said `none`, and is superseded), Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes.
- ⛔ Still running, so not yet a verdict: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, all four Type Check jobs, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus.
- This record judges the contract and the design. It does not stand in for the running gates: the behavioural pins (hint equals the prescription, head on the wire) are answered by Test Core, which has not reported.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Status and code: unchanged. Right.** `zodIssuesToFields` computes `code` from the issue exactly as before; the only new input on an issue is `params.refusalHead`, and nothing in the mapper or `zodIssueToFieldCode` reads `params`. `withRefusalHeadAnswer` rebuilds the body with the same `status` and spreads the same body, replacing `error` and merging `details.hint` only. No request is refused that was accepted, and none is accepted that was refused: the schemas, the comparand face's conditions and the save-door walk's conditions are untouched. No narrowing.
- **Accepted values: one, a widening.** `FieldErrorSchema` gains `hint: z.string().optional()` on a non-strict `z.object`. A parser on the previous published schema strips an unknown `hint`; a parser on the new one accepts a body without it. Non-breaking both ways. The schema is embedded in other published schemas (the regenerated `errors.mdx` and `push-relay.mdx` show five tables gaining the row), and the same holds for each.
- **`message` / `error` text: shorter on headed refusals, same otherwise. Right, and declared.** An unheaded issue maps with no `hint` member and its old `message`.
- **`details.hint` on a thrown 4xx: right.** `details` is `unknown` on the envelope, the merge keeps existing members, and 5xx, a non-string `error` and an unheaded error are returned as they were.
- **New spec exports: `refusalHeadOf` and `REFUSAL_HEAD_MAX` from `@objectstack/spec/api`. Right.** `@objectstack/types` needs the reader, and it sits beside `zodIssuesToFields`, which is already exported there for the same consumer. `withRefusalHead`, `assertRefusalHead` and `headFieldName` stay internal. `api-surface/api.json` and `export-origins/api.json` carry exactly those two names with the origin `src/shared/refusal-head.ts`; `authorable-surface/api.json` carries exactly `api/FieldError:hint`. The three generated files agree with the source.
- **The analytics selection door: in the diff's reach, declared in the PR body, not in the changeset.** See ④ should-fix 1: it is one of several doors the shared mapper reaches.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset on `508fb649`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/types` patch, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. The PR body carries the same two lines and a note on why the declaration moved.
- This matches what the diff publishes. `api/FieldError:hint` enters `authorable-surface`, which the ratchet reads as a key added, so `added` and at least `minor` on spec is what AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 and the gate require. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- The brief's premise (`Metadata-protocol: none`, so patch) was wrong for this diff and is corrected on the card by 6777418296. The card body still says `none`; the correction comment governs.
- `@objectstack/types` at patch is right: it gains no key and changes no accepted value.
- Both packages the diff moves are named. No `major`, no BREAKING banner owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations in the os-dev-report:
1. **File surface widened to `zod-issues-to-fields.ts`, `api/index.ts`, new `shared/refusal-head.ts`.** Accepted. The claim's surface named "the `packages/types` / `packages/rest` mappers that carry the hint", and the mapper those call lives in spec. Carrying the hint anywhere else would need a second copy.
2. **Whole prescription kept as `hint`, not "the rest".** Accepted. It is what keeps the authoring text byte-equal with one source.
3. **Four rest reader pins moved from `message` to `hint`.** Lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; not judged here.
4. **Analytics selection door answers the same heads.** Accepted as a consequence, but under-declared: see ④ should-fix 1.
5. **`find('…'):` leads the head only when both fit in 160.** Accepted. The hint keeps the context either way.
6. **`origin/main` moved after the merge.** No effect on these files.

`open_questions`: none raised. `security_findings`: the dev reports none; I found none. `out_of_scope_findings` (other long refusals left unheaded): a follow-up card, not this PR's.

Escalated: nothing.

### ④ Design judgment

Per `hits` file:

- **`errors.zod.ts`**: holds. One optional string, described, on a non-strict object.
- **`api/index.ts`**: holds. Two names, both needed by `@objectstack/types`.
- **`zod-issues-to-fields.ts`**: holds. `hint` is `String(issue.message)`, the exact string that was `message` before, so the hint is byte-equal to the old answer by construction. The head replaces `message` only when `refusalHeadOf` returns a one-line string within the bound.
- **`query.zod.ts`**: holds. `withRefusalHead` returns its first argument, so each of the six constants keeps its text, and the two exported ones keep type `string`. Head lengths by count: `array_agg` 133, `string_agg` 134, `aggregations[].distinct` 131, `joins` 108, `cursor` 118, `distinct` 135. Each names the refused key and the fix.
- **`filter-comparand-shape.ts`**: holds. The thrown message is built exactly as before; `refusalHead` is an added own property. A head that is blank, multi-line or over the bound is dropped, never thrown, so a refusal cannot become a fault. With the field elided at 40 characters the longest heads I count are 153 (`$between` with a `$field` endpoint) and 152 (blank bound); all eleven arms are within 160 and each names operator, field and fix.
- **`filter-save-door-refusals.ts`**: holds. The issue's `message` and `path` are unchanged; the head rides in `params`. The face is called without a context there, so the save door's head carries no `find(…)` prefix.
- **`refusal-head.ts`**: holds. One reader, three carriers, one bound. No second copy of any head or prescription exists in the diff: heads are written once beside their prescription, and `rest` holds no text.

Implementing files:

- **`data-error-classification.ts`**: agrees with the contract. Composed into `withDeclaredUserMessage`, so every exit that renders a thrown sentence gets the same answer. The 4xx sentence it moves to `details.hint` was already addressed to the caller, so nothing withheld becomes visible.
- **`validation-failure.ts`**: agrees. Return type widened by an optional member; `withoutDateRangeArityRestatement` spreads the issue, so `params` survives.

Authoring surfaces: `os compile`, `os migrate meta` and the MCP parameter renderer print through `formatZodIssue` / `formatZodError`, which read `message` only; the metadata save doors map through `zodIssuesToMetadataIssues`, which also reads `message` only. Both print what they printed. This is by reading; the pins that prove it run in Test Core.

Findings:

1. **should-fix (changeset and PR body, prose).** The changeset names two doors. The shared mapper has more callers, and each now answers head plus hint for the same refusals: the batch and bulk routes, the record-page route, the analytics selection door (whose top-level `message` is composed from `fields[].message`, so it now carries heads), the runtime dispatcher's data and analytics domains, the dataset tools (their composed `message` likewise) and the `sys_personal_view` save hook in `plugin-auth`. The last one is a save door for a `ListView` whose `fields[].message` is now the head, so "the save doors print the prescription byte for byte as before" is true of the metadata save doors and not of that one (its prescription moved to `hint`). The behaviour is consistent and is what the card asks for; the published note should say the change applies to every door that answers `fields[]` through `zodIssuesToFields`, and name the personal-view save.
2. **nit.** `refusal-head.ts` says the longest comparand head is the `$notContains` list arm at 151; by count it is the `$between` field-reference arm at 153. Still within the bound.
3. **nit.** `headFieldName` cuts at 39 UTF-16 units and can split a surrogate pair in a field name.
4. **nit.** The mapper's de-duplication key uses the answered `message`, now the head. Two branch issues at one field with one head and different prescriptions collapse to the first.
5. **nit.** Doors that answer raw zod `issues` (`rest` `error-response.ts`, `batch-routes.ts` line 260) now show `params.refusalHead` on a save-door-walk issue. Additive.
6. **nit.** `withRefusalHeadAnswer`'s comment names the comparand face only, but `refusalHeadOf` also matches a thrown error whose message equals a registered prescription. No producer throws one today (the engine's option refusal embeds the constant in a longer sentence).
7. **nit.** `withRefusalHead` registers on `globalThis` at module load in a package marked `sideEffects: false`. It holds because each constant's value is the call's return, so the call cannot be dropped while the constant is used.

Nits 2 to 7 are left as accepted deviations or a follow-up card; fixing them in code moves the head. Should-fix 1 is a changeset and PR-body edit and earns a delta review of the new head.
